label: Existential receptivity: a principle open to a thing's being, received esse or matter and form
definition: ExistentiallyReceptive esseOf Received ReceptivePotencyTo ComposedOfMatterAndForm x: x has a principle open to its being. Either the esse of x is received in some principle p that stands in receptive potency to that esse (Received x p and ReceptivePotencyTo p (esseOf x): the receiver and received act of De ente c.3, DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN and DEF-RECEPTIVE-POTENCY), or x is composed of matter and form (the ComposedOfMatterAndForm parameter of the existing simplicity reading; matter is receptive of substantial form, Met. Theta.8 1050b, navigation only). A defined disjunction over those parameters; it asserts no cause, no modality and no POTENCY_1.
note: Stipulated for C2 (docs/notes/contingency-receptivity-c2.md) as the 'relevant receptive potency' of a contingent being. Examples: on the Thomist account, an angel (its esse received in its quiddity) and a dog (received esse, and matter and form); on a Suarezian account without a real essence-esse distinction, a corruptible body (matter and form). Non-examples: a being whose esse is identical with its essence and received in nothing, with no matter (the First Way's mover under the simplicity and reception premises); and a being merely able to become hot, which is in POTENCY_1 (DEF-POTENCY, CanBe and not InAct) in a respect without thereby having a principle open to its being. Distinct from POTENCY_1 at esse: by the R2 law of the First Way reception controls, unactualized POTENCY_1 at esse is incompatible with actual existence, whereas a receiving principle may already have its act. Distinct from RECEPTIVE_POTENCY_1 alone: it adds the matter-form disjunct and is predicated of the bearer, not of a principle. Open obligations: whether matter's receptivity to form and a principle's receptivity to esse are one kind of openness to being (the passive-to-receptive bridge treats them as alternatives, not as one sense); whether reception of esse is a real constitution of its bearer (open at DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN). What would source it: a passage treating the two receptivities together as what makes a thing able not to be.
